elicitation_rationale: All 6 confidence criteria are met from the initial request. The user specified technology (Redis, token bucket), exact rates (5/min, 100/min, unlimited), HTTP behavior (429 + Retry-After), integration points (src/config/redis.ts, src/middleware/), and the middleware pattern (Express). Asking further questions would be over-elicitation. Minor implementation details (rate limit key strategy, fail-open vs fail-closed) are appropriately deferred to the architect phase.
feature_spec_summary: Rate limiting Express middleware with per-route configuration (unlimited for /health, 5/min for auth, 100/min for general API), using Redis-backed token bucket counters via existing src/config/redis.ts connection, returning 429 with Retry-After header, integrated into existing src/middleware/ chain alongside auth middleware.

explorer_focuses.description: Trace the existing middleware chain in src/middleware/. Understand how auth middleware is registered, what patterns it follows (factory functions, configuration objects, error handling). Map middleware ordering and how routes apply middleware.

Analyze src/config/redis.ts — how the Redis client is created, exported, and used across the codebase. Look for existing patterns of Redis usage (caching, sessions) that the rate limiter should follow. Check for Redis Lua script patterns and error handling.

Map Express route definitions to understand how per-route middleware is applied. Identify all route groups (auth, health, general). Look for existing per-route configuration patterns and middleware test patterns.
